mainTopic: Immersing (טבילה) on שבת, יום טוב and יום הכיפורים, רבא's 'since' reasoning, and purifying water and vessels on יום טוב
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why one may immerse (טבילה) on שבת and יום טוב: it doesn't clearly look like purifying, because people sometimes bathe just to cool off. It then tests this answer. In the rainy season nobody bathes to cool off, but רב נחמן בר יצחק says people also wash off mud and filth. On יום הכיפורים all ordinary bathing is forbidden, so רבא gives a rule instead: whatever is allowed on שבת is also allowed on יום הכיפורים. The גמרא asks whether רבא really uses this kind of 'since' (הואיל) reasoning, because in the case of vinegar for a toothache he did not. It concludes that רבא took back his vinegar answer, and a ברייתא confirms that טבילה is allowed on יום הכיפורים and תשעה באב. Then the גמרא turns to a line of the משנה about purifying water in a stone vessel. שמואל explains that one may not immerse an impure vessel together with its water on יום טוב. This reading seems to match neither רבי nor the חכמים, and the גמרא begins to show that it can fit רבי by placing his two rulings on יום טוב and שבת. The answer that follows the חכמים comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A person may bathe in a heat wave, even in foul water
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the earlier answer: a person sometimes gets so hot that he bathes even in smelly flax-soaking water.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Sometimes a person is hot] in a heat wave, and he washes even in the foul water used for soaking flax.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that began before this section. It explains why טבילה on שבת doesn't look like 'fixing' a person: people sometimes bathe just to cool off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that טבילה looks like מתקן, making a person טהור, which resembles fixing something on שבת. The answer is that an onlooker can't tell it is for טהרה, since a hot person will jump into any water, even dirty water, just to cool down. If he'd use even foul water, then going into a מקוה looks like cooling off too.

keyTerms.meaning: Water used for soaking flax; dirty and smelly

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the end of a sentence that started earlier, explaining that טבילה looks like bathing for comfort, not like purifying.

phrases.english: in a heat wave,
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier sentence: 'Sometimes a person is hot...' The beginning is just before this section.

phrases.english: and he washes even in flax-soaking water.
phrases.notes: Flax was soaked in water to soften it, which left the water smelly. Only a really hot person would bathe in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun before this section, which explains why טבילה on שבת is not seen as מתקן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the act: it looks like bathing for comfort
steps.terutzHavaAmina: טבילה on שבת looks like making oneself טהור, which is like fixing something
steps.terutzMaskana: People bathe just to cool off, even in dirty water, so טבילה does not clearly look like purifying

steps.title: What about the rainy season?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: in winter nobody bathes to cool off, so טבילה would clearly look like purifying.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well in the summer. But in the rainy season, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. The 'cooling off' reason only works in hot weather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on people bathing for comfort in the heat. In winter that reason doesn't apply, so an onlooker would assume the person is immersing for טהרה. The answer seems too narrow to explain why טבילה is allowed all year.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That works fine'; it grants one case and sets up a challenge on another
'What is there to say?'; asking for an answer to a hard case

phrases.english: This works well in the summer season;
in the rainy season, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה, בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'cooling off' answer of Step 1 as limited to summer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that טבילה looks like bathing to cool off
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the rainy season no one bathes for heat, so טבילה would clearly look like it is for טהרה.

steps.title: People wash off mud and filth even in winter
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that even in winter a person may come home dirty from the field and wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Sometimes a person comes from the field covered in mud and filth, and he washes even in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the winter challenge with a different everyday reason for bathing: getting clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for bathing doesn't have to be heat; it can be dirt. Since people wash off mud all year round, an onlooker still can't tell that a winter טבילה is for טהרה, so the original idea holds.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Sometimes a person comes from the field
soiled with mud and excrement,
and washes even in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם בָּא מִן הַשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the winter challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a second ordinary reason for bathing that applies all year
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In winter, טבילה could only look like it is for טהרה
steps.terutzMaskana: People wash off dirt even in winter, so טבילה still looks like ordinary bathing

steps.title: What about יום הכיפורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: on יום הכיפורים all ordinary bathing is forbidden, so any immersion clearly looks like it is for טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well on שבת. But on יום הכיפורים, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a harder case. The 'it looks like regular bathing' answer works for שבת, but not for יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, washing for comfort or cleanliness is allowed, so a person in the water looks like an ordinary bather. On יום הכיפורים, רחיצה (bathing) itself is forbidden, so anyone seen immersing must be doing it for טהרה. The disguise falls away, and it should look like מתקן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement, when bathing for pleasure is forbidden
The Sabbath, when washing is allowed

phrases.english: This works well on Shabbat;
on Yom Kippur, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: Ordinary bathing is forbidden on יום הכיפורים, so nobody could think he is just washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּשַׁבָּת, בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the winter problem was solved, the גמרא attacks the same answer from a new angle: a day when no bathing is allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The whole 'it looks like ordinary bathing' explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום הכיפורים no one bathes for comfort or cleanliness, so immersion clearly looks like it is for טהרה and should be forbidden.

steps.title: Whatever is allowed on שבת is allowed on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the חכמים never forbid on יום הכיפורים something they allowed on שבת, so טבילה is allowed on יום הכיפורים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is there anything that is allowed on שבת but forbidden on יום הכיפורים? Rather, since it is allowed on שבת, it is also allowed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not find a new reason the immersion looks innocent on יום הכיפורים. Instead, he gives a general rule: יום הכיפורים cannot be stricter than שבת about these things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is the more severe day for forbidden work, so it makes no sense for an act allowed on שבת to be forbidden on יום הכיפורים. Since the חכמים allowed טבילה on שבת, they did not single out יום הכיפורים for a stricter rule. This holds even though on יום הכיפורים the immersion clearly is for טהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is there anything...?'; a rhetorical question meaning 'there is no such thing'

steps.whatToRemember: טבילה on שבת is allowed because it looks like ordinary bathing, whether to cool off in summer or to wash off dirt in winter. On יום הכיפורים that reason doesn't work, but רבא's rule applies: what is allowed on שבת is also allowed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the immersion on יום הכיפורים looks like regular bathing. He agrees it doesn't, and allows it anyway because of the rule that יום הכיפורים follows שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a principle of how the חכמים made their rules: they kept יום הכיפורים in line with שבת and did not make it stricter on these matters.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is there anything that is permitted on Shabbat
and prohibited on Yom Kippur?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. He means there's no such thing, since שבת is the stricter day.

phrases.english: Rather, since it is permitted on Shabbat,
it is also permitted on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּבְשַׁבָּת שְׁרֵי וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יום הכיפורים challenge of Step 4 with a general principle instead of a new explanation of how it looks.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle linking the rules of יום הכיפורים to those of שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: On יום הכיפורים, טבילה obviously looks like it is for טהרה, so it should be forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Nothing allowed on שבת is forbidden on יום הכיפורים; since טבילה is allowed on שבת, it is allowed on יום הכיפורים

steps.title: Does רבא really use the since argument? The toothache case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבא accepts הואיל reasoning and begins by quoting a משנה about vinegar for a toothache on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבא really hold of "since"? But we learned in a משנה: someone with a toothache may not sip vinegar through his teeth on שבת, but he may dip his food in it the normal way, and if he gets healed, he gets healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רבא's answer from step 5. Here it is only setting up the challenge by quoting a משנה; the actual attack comes a few steps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer was a הואיל argument: since טבילה is allowed on שבת, it is allowed on יום הכיפורים. The גמרא wants to show a place where רבא seems not to use that kind of reasoning. The משנה forbids sipping vinegar, which looks like medicine, but allows dipping food in it the normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: "Since": the reasoning that because something is allowed in one setting, it is also allowed in a related one
Someone who has pain in his teeth

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about vinegar for its own sake. The גמרא brings the vinegar case only to test whether רבא is consistent about the "since" reasoning he just used for טבילה.

phrases.english: And does Rava hold of "since"?
phrases.notes: This refers to רבא's answer just before: since it is allowed on שבת, it is allowed on יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: one who has pain in his teeth
may not sip vinegar through them,
phrases.notes: This is on שבת. Sipping would look like he is taking medicine.

phrases.english: but he may dip his food in the usual way,
and if he is healed, he is healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning method behind רבא's answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of הואיל to allow טבילה on יום הכיפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא elsewhere refuses to use "since" reasoning, his ruling about יום הכיפורים is inconsistent. The vinegar case is being set up to show this.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts the toothache משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier contradiction: a ברייתא allows sipping vinegar and swallowing it, which seems to argue with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we raised a contradiction to this משנה: one may not sip and spit out, but one may sip and swallow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reminds us of an older contradiction about the vinegar משנה. It is still setting the stage for the challenge against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to forbid sipping vinegar entirely. The ברייתא forbids only sipping and spitting, which clearly looks like medicine. It allows sipping and swallowing, which looks like normal drinking. The two sources seem to disagree.

phrases.english: And we raised a contradiction against it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the vinegar משנה. The contradiction comes from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: one may not sip and spit out,
but one may sip and swallow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the ברייתא that contradicts the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ban on sipping vinegar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows sipping and swallowing, while the משנה seems to forbid all sipping.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה means sipping and spitting
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the contradiction by explaining that the משנה also forbids only sipping and spitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: when we learned the משנה too, it was talking about sipping and spitting out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his answer to the contradiction. He says the משנה and the ברייתא actually agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the משנה's "may not sip" means sipping and spitting, which is clearly for healing. Sipping and swallowing is allowed by both sources, so there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
When we learned the mishnah too,
we learned it about sipping and spitting out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר אַבָּיֵי כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids every kind of sipping.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids only sipping and spitting, just like the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: before dipping versus after dipping
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently. Sipping before dipping food is allowed, and sipping after dipping is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: even if you say the משנה forbids sipping and swallowing, it is not difficult. Here it is before dipping, there it is after dipping.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the contradiction. This is the answer the גמרא will use against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps the משנה's ban on sipping and swallowing too, and splits the cases by timing. Before he dips his food, sipping looks like enjoying the vinegar, so the ברייתא allows it. After he has already dipped, sipping looks like it is only for his tooth, so the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there: splitting two sources into two different cases

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even if you say it means sipping and swallowing,
phrases.notes: He means: even if the משנה forbids sipping and swallowing too.

phrases.english: it is still not difficult:
here it is before dipping,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the ברייתא, which allows sipping before he dips his food.

phrases.english: there it is after dipping.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מְגַמֵּעַ וּבוֹלֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same contradiction that אביי answered in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources into two cases (before and after dipping)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא argue about sipping and swallowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sipping before dipping is allowed. Sipping after dipping is forbidden.

steps.title: Why didn't רבא say since it is allowed before, it is allowed after?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. If רבא held of הואיל, he should have allowed sipping after dipping too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so that he holds of "since," let him say: since sipping is allowed before dipping, it is also allowed after dipping!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual punch of the challenge that began in step 6. רבא's vinegar answer seems to reject "since" reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For יום הכיפורים, רבא said that what is allowed on שבת is allowed on יום הכיפורים, even though it looks worse there. By the same logic, what is allowed before dipping should be allowed after dipping. Yet רבא forbade it, so he seems inconsistent.

phrases.english: And if it is so, let him say:
phrases.notes: "If it is so" means: if רבא really holds of "since."

phrases.english: since before dipping it is permitted,
after dipping it should also be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's answer from step 9 to complete the challenge opened in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency between רבא's טבילה ruling (step 5) and his vinegar answer (step 9)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he uses הואיל for יום הכיפורים, he should also use it for sipping vinegar after dipping. He did not, so the two rulings contradict each other.

steps.title: רבא took back his vinegar answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא retracted his before-and-after-dipping answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying רבא changed his mind about one of his two statements, namely the vinegar answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבא drops his vinegar answer, he no longer has a ruling that rejects "since." He stays with the הואיל reasoning for טבילה on יום הכיפורים, and for the vinegar case he accepts אביי's answer.

phrases.english: Rava retracted from that one.
phrases.notes: "That one" is his vinegar answer about before and after dipping.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction of one of the two conflicting statements
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds both rulings, and they seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא dropped the vinegar answer and keeps הואיל.

steps.title: How do we know which statement he took back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we assume רבא retracted the vinegar answer. Maybe he retracted the טבילה ruling instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he retracted that one? Maybe he retracted this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 11 by asking how we know which of רבא's two statements was dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two statements that clash, so either one could be the one he retracted. If he dropped the יום הכיפורים ruling, his reason for allowing טבילה on יום הכיפורים would be gone. The next step shows why that cannot be.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he retracted from that one,
perhaps he retracted from this one?
phrases.notes: "This one" is his ruling that טבילה is allowed on יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption in step 11 about which statement was retracted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that רבא dropped the vinegar answer and not the טבילה ruling.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows טבילה on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבא kept his טבילה ruling, because a ברייתא clearly allows טבילה on תשעה באב and יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, for it is taught in a ברייתא: all who need to immerse may immerse in their usual way, both on תשעה באב and on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12 with a ברייתא. It shows that the טבילה ruling could not be the one רבא gave up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright that people who need טבילה may immerse on יום הכיפורים, even though washing is forbidden that day. רבא would not take back a ruling that a ברייתא supports, so he must have dropped the vinegar answer instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't think that; it cannot be
People who are required to immerse
The Ninth of Av, a fast day when washing is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds of הואיל: since טבילה is allowed on שבת, it is allowed on יום הכיפורים, and a ברייתא backs this up. He gave up his before-and-after-dipping answer in the vinegar case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה: someone who needs טבילה may immerse in the normal way on יום הכיפורים and on תשעה באב, even though ordinary washing is forbidden then.

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind, as it is taught:
all who are obligated in immersions immerse in their usual way,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב בֵּין בְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: both on the Ninth of Av and on Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: These are both days when ordinary washing is forbidden, yet טבילה is still allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא allows טבילה on יום הכיפורים, so רבא kept that ruling and dropped the vinegar answer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: כל חייבי טבילות טובלין כדרכן, בין בתשעה באב בין ביום הכיפורים
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טבילה is allowed on יום הכיפורים, and רבא holds of הואיל.

steps.title: What does 'but one may not immerse' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about purifying water in a stone vessel and asks what the words 'but one may not immerse' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that everyone agrees you may bring impure water into contact with pure water in a stone vessel. What does it mean when it adds, 'but one may not immerse'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It asks what the משנה's limit, 'but one may not immerse,' is talking about. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows השקה, which purifies impure water by letting it touch a מקוה or pure water. Then it says 'but one may not immerse' without telling us what may not be immersed. The גמרא wants that detail filled in.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (בית שמאי and בית הלל both hold this)
Bringing impure water into contact with pure water to purify it (השקה)
A stone vessel, which cannot become טמא
Immersing something in a מקוה to purify it

phrases.english: And they agree that one may bring the water into contact
phrases.notes: This means impure water touching pure water. That contact makes the impure water pure.

phrases.english: in a stone vessel, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה's line: 'but one may not immerse.'

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "but one may not immerse"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבא discussion about טבילה and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the משנה forbids immersing on יום טוב.

steps.title: שמואל: no immersing a vessel with its water
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה forbids immersing an impure vessel along with its water in order to purify it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: On יום טוב, you may not immerse an impure vessel, using its water as the reason, in order to make the vessel pure.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The forbidden 'immersing' is dipping an impure vessel full of water into a מקוה, which would also purify the vessel itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making water pure for drinking on יום טוב is allowed. But here the vessel would also become pure, and making a vessel pure looks like 'fixing' it, so it is forbidden. A stone vessel avoids this problem, since it was never impure in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of its water: the vessel is immersed together with the water inside it

steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's reading is the base for the whole challenge that follows. It is the reason the משנה seems to clash with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One may not immerse the vessel
on account of its water
phrases.notes: Picture an impure pot filled with water and dipped into the מקוה. You do it for the water, but the pot gets purified too.

phrases.english: to purify it on a Festival.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה forbids immersing an impure vessel together with its water, because that purifies the vessel on יום טוב.

steps.title: The משנה seems to fit neither רבי nor the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי forbids both immersing and השקה, while the חכמים allow both. The משנה, as שמואל read it, allows one and forbids the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is the משנה? Not רבי's and not the חכמים'. A ברייתא teaches: You may not immerse a vessel with its water to purify it, and you may not touch water to pure water in a stone vessel to purify it. That is רבי's view. The חכמים say: You may immerse a vessel with its water to purify it, and you may touch water to pure water in a stone vessel to purify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה (as שמואל explained it). It quotes a ברייתא with two opinions, and neither one matches the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, each side treats the two actions the same way. רבי forbids both, and the חכמים allow both. The משנה splits them: השקה is allowed, but immersing the vessel is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two actions separate. השקה means touching water to pure water while it sits in a stone vessel. טבילה here means dipping an impure vessel with its water into the מקוה.

phrases.english: In accordance with whose opinion is the mishna?
Not Rabbi and not the Rabbis,
as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַטְבִּילִין אֶת הַכְּלִי עַל גַּב מֵימָיו לְטַהֲרוֹ,
phrases.english: One may not immerse the vessel on account of its water to purify it,
and one may not bring the water into contact
in a stone vessel to purify it,
these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: מַטְבִּילִין כְּלִי עַל גַּב מֵימָיו לְטַהֲרוֹ,
phrases.english: One may immerse a vessel on account of its water to purify it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַשִּׁיקִין אֶת הַמַּיִם בִּכְלִי אֶבֶן לְטַהֲרָן.
phrases.english: and one may bring the water into contact in a stone vessel to purify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא רַבִּי וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's reading to show that the משנה does not match the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה as explained by שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats immersing and השקה the same way (both forbidden or both allowed), but the משנה splits them, so no known opinion fits.

steps.title: Spelling out the clash on each side
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי, its permission for השקה is a problem. If it follows the חכמים, its ban on immersing is a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is it? If it is רבי's, the השקה ruling is a problem. If it is the חכמים', the immersion ruling is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. It shows exactly which part of the משנה clashes with each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי forbids השקה, but the משנה allows it. The חכמים allow immersing the vessel, but the משנה forbids it. Each option breaks one half of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing impure water into contact with pure water

phrases.english: Whose is it?
If Rabbi, bringing into contact is difficult,
if the Rabbis, immersion is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי קַשְׁיָא הַשָּׁקָה, אִי רַבָּנַן קַשְׁיָא הַטְבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the exact clash behind the challenge in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: Matching the משנה to either side of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side contradicts one half of the משנה: רבי contradicts its השקה ruling, and the חכמים contradict its immersion ruling.

steps.title: The משנה can follow רבי: his rulings cover יום טוב and שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow either side. According to רבי, his first ruling is about יום טוב, his second is about שבת, and the משנה is about יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבי, and if you want, say it follows the חכמים. If you want to say רבי: the first part of the ברייתא is about יום טוב, the second part is about שבת, and the whole משנה is about יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה can fit either side. Here it explains the first way, matching the משנה to רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's ban on immersing a vessel applies even on יום טוב. His ban on השקה applies only on שבת, which is stricter. Since the משנה is about יום טוב, it can forbid immersing and allow השקה, just like רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (one possible answer)
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי: immersing a vessel with its water is forbidden even on יום טוב, but השקה is forbidden only on שבת. So the משנה (about יום טוב) matches רבי.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is Rabbi,
if you wish, say it is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The answer that matches the חכמים comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is Rabbi:
the first clause of the baraita is on a Festival,
phrases.notes: This is רבי's ban on immersing the vessel with its water.

phrases.english: and the latter clause is on Shabbat,
and the entire mishna is on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 16 and 17 by splitting רבי's two rulings between יום טוב and שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the clauses of the ברייתא between different days
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's two bans in the ברייתא both apply on the same day, so he forbids השקה even on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי forbids immersing even on יום טוב but forbids השקה only on שבת, so the משנה about יום טוב fits רבי.
